initial_plan.answerability: partly: the file can show annual counts of reported pedestrian deaths in Brooklyn, but not a population- or walking-exposure-adjusted road-safety rate or causation
initial_plan.metric: annual number of pedestrians reported killed in Brooklyn motor-vehicle crashes
initial_plan.denominator: calendar year; this is a count, not a rate
initial_plan.population: people recorded as pedestrians killed in police-reported crashes with borough Brooklyn and a crash date in a calendar year from 2013 onward
filters: use complete calendar years only if coverage checks show the latest year is partial
initial_plan.years: 2013 through the latest covered calendar year, restricted to complete years after the data check

data_check_implications_and_decisions.population_rows: 483,501 Brooklyn crash records from 2013 onward have the pedestrian-killed field available; 2013–2025 have full observed date bounds, while 2026 is observed only through June 11 and is excluded to avoid comparing a partial year with full years.
data_check_implications_and_decisions.borough: Among all 2,168,642 crashes with a nonmissing date from 2013 onward, 668,406 (30.821408%) have borough missing or labeled unknown. Such records cannot be assigned to Brooklyn; exclude them from the Brooklyn count and disclose this coverage limitation. Brooklyn rows are selected by a nonblank borough value equal to Brooklyn.
data_check_implications_and_decisions.outcome: In the Brooklyn population, the integer pedestrian-killed field has 0 NULLs, 0 impossible negative values, and no text missing values are possible by type. Zero is the expected no-death default for 483,119/483,501 (99.920993%) crash records; retain these valid zeros in the underlying population.
data_check_implications_and_decisions.crash_date: There are 0 missing crash dates, so none are unassignable to a year.
data_check_implications_and_decisions.changes: Restrict the analysis to complete years 2013–2025; retain zero fatality values; exclude borough-missing and non-Brooklyn records because their location cannot support a Brooklyn assignment.

final_plan.answerability: partly: compare reported pedestrian death counts over time, but the data cannot establish a true safety rate because pedestrian exposure is absent, nor attribute trends causally
final_plan.metric: annual number of pedestrians reported killed in Brooklyn motor-vehicle crashes
final_plan.denominator: calendar year; annual count, not a rate
final_plan.population: pedestrians reported killed in police-reported crashes with borough Brooklyn and crash dates from January 1, 2013 through December 31, 2025
filters: retain zero values in pedestrian-killed field
final_plan.limitations: Counts of reported deaths are not exposure-adjusted safety rates; the data has no pedestrian-trip or population denominator. Of all date-eligible NYC records from 2013 onward, 668,406/2,168,642 (30.821408%) lack a usable borough and cannot be assigned to Brooklyn. The partial 2026 period (through June 11) is excluded; zero pedestrian-death values are retained as valid no-death crash records.
